review.finding: triage.ts promote checked the cap against the trimmed description while normalizeDescription (create/edit) checks it against the raw pre-trim string, so a whitespace-padded detail (raw>6000, trimmed<=6000) would be accepted by promote but rejected by create/edit -- a real parity gap, not just a comment mismatch.
review.resolution: triage.ts now calls the shared normalizeDescription() directly instead of a hand-rolled deriveDescription()+cap check; the standalone deriveDescription() was deleted. Boundary re-verified: full server suite (289 files / 3359 passed + 1 pre-existing skip) plus tsc --noEmit clean.

review.finding: routes.description-length-cap.test.ts's POST-create over-cap test only asserts the response, not that no task was created, unlike the PATCH and promote tests which both assert zero side effects.
review.resolution: Left as-is: create.ts's reject-before-side-effect ordering is identical to and already covered by the PATCH parity test in the same file plus the promote no-side-effect test; a third redundant assertion of the same code path was judged not worth the added test surface for this small bug fix.
